concepts.title: What an Essay Is
concepts.definition: An essay is a short composition in prose that undertakes to discuss a matter, express a point of view, or persuade us to accept a thesis. Its family name, from Montaigne's 'essai' or attempt, marks it as exploratory -- an intelligence trying out its thoughts on paper.
concepts.key_idea: An essay is an attempt in prose -- a mind thinking on paper to discuss, persuade or express.
concepts.textbook_ref: keww131.txt introduction (essay as short composition in prose, discuss a matter, express a point of view, persuade, montaigne attempt)
question_patterns: define an essay and explain its origin
in class 11 essays introduction: what are the purposes an essay can serve
why is the essay called an attempt or trial
distinguish an essay that discusses from one that persuades
what does prose composition imply about the essay form
name the essayist credited with founding the essay form

solution_steps.explain: Brevity, prose and a single governing matter define the essay against longer, more varied works.
An essay may discuss, express or persuade -- three registers of the same prose instrument.
Montaigne's essais -- attempts -- gave the form its exploratory name and manner.

concepts.title: Types of Essays: Formal and Informal
concepts.definition: Essays divide into formal and informal. The formal essay treats serious subjects with organised argument and impersonal tone; the informal or familiar essay is conversational, personal and light, sharing the essayist's moods and whimsies as if talking with a friend.
concepts.key_idea: Two voices of the same form -- the lecture hall's formality, the fireside's familiar chat.
concepts.textbook_ref: keww131.txt types sections (formal essay, informal or familiar essay, tone and organisation, charles lamb mention)
question_patterns: distinguish formal essays from informal essays
in class 11 essays introduction: what is a familiar essay
which type of essay uses impersonal argument and which uses personal chat
give examples of subjects suited to formal and informal essays
why is the informal essay compared to conversation
match given essay titles to formal or informal type

solution_steps.explain: Serious subject, structured argument, impersonal voice -- the formal essay argues its case.
Everyday subject, rambling charm, personal voice -- the familiar essay confides in its reader.
Most real essays move between the poles, blending argument with personality.

concepts.title: Reading the Essays of This Section
concepts.definition: The section gathers four essays of very different temper -- Russell's passionate autobiography of passions, Chandrasekhar's meditation on creativity and science, Devy's defence of tribal expression, and Ruskin's discriminating theory of the good book -- showing the essay's power to argue, personalise, defend and evaluate.
concepts.key_idea: One form, four tempers -- passion, science, advocacy and criticism displayed in four essays.
concepts.textbook_ref: keww131.txt preview sections (bertrand russell my three passions, chandrasekhar patterns of creativity, devy tribal verse, ruskin what is a good book)
question_patterns: name the essays and essayists included in this section
in class 11 essays introduction: what theme unites russell's essay
which essay deals with science and creativity
what subject does g n devy's essay defend
what standard does ruskin propose in his essay
compare the temper of any two essays in the section

solution_steps.explain: Russell, Chandrasekhar, Devy and Ruskin head the section's contents.
Personal passion, scientific biography, cultural advocacy and aesthetic criticism -- four distinct essayistic modes.
Reading across them teaches how one prose form can carry many intellectual tempers.

worked_examples.question_pattern: Classify these subjects into formal and informal essays: 'The Evils of War', 'My First Umbrella', 'On Saying Please', 'Confessions of a Glutton'.

solution_template.explain: War and social courtesy ('On Saying Please') invite organised argument -- formal essays.
Umbrellas and gluttony invite personal whim and anecdote -- familiar essays.
Even light subjects can be treated formally -- the treatment, not the topic, decides.

worked_examples.question_pattern: Why did Montaigne call his prose pieces 'essais'? What does the name promise the reader?

solution_template.explain: Essai means attempt or trial in French.
The reader is offered a mind testing its thoughts, not delivering verdicts from on high.
The essay's modest name is its honest contract: exploration, not finality.
